- **Limitations:** Does not reflect real-world performance because it ignores the significant computational cost of extracting the isosurface and determining visibility (occlusion culling) [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that the evidence does not reflect real-world performance because it ignores the computational cost of extracting the isosurface and determining visibility (occlusion culling). The provided text from Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly supports this. Specifically, the 'Optimized Mesh Reference' section in both sources states that the reference 'does not consider time taken for geometry extraction and occlusion culling' and represents an 'infinitely fast indirect isosurface extraction approach.' Furthermore, the text notes that for a real-world comparison, 'the time taken to extract the explicit isosurface representation would need to be added to the presented rendering times.' Thus, every fact in the claim is present in the evidence.
supported

This method serves as an upper bound for forward mesh rendering efficiency, allowing researchers to assess how close a practical pipeline comes to the theoretical limit of rendering an optimized isosurface [S1][S2, unofficial].

The evidence in both Source [S1] and Source [S2] explicitly states that the 'Optimized Mesh Reference' serves as a comparison against an 'ideal indirect isosurface visualization technique' to 'assess how close our approach comes to the best possible performance.' It describes this method as rendering a 'highly-optimized mesh representation' without accounting for geometry extraction or occlusion culling overhead, which effectively represents the 'theoretical limit' or 'upper bound' for forward mesh rendering of an optimized isosurface. The claim accurately reflects these descriptions.

The method relies on the `meshoptimizer` library by Kapoulkine [S1][S2, unofficial] and follows recommendations by Kubisch regarding meshlet sizes [S1][S2, unofficial].

The evidence explicitly states in both Source [S1] and Source [S2] that the isosurface extraction approach uses 'Kapoulkine's meshoptimizer C++ library' to create meshlets. Furthermore, both sources confirm that this process follows 'Kubisch's [Kub18] recommendation for default meshlet sizes' and limits each meshlet to at most 64 vertices. All factual components of the claim are present in the provided text.
